Scallops

Time: 10min
Servings: 2
Source: Chefparade
Tags: tested, savory, snack, main-course, medium-effort, fish, gluten-free, milk-free

Ingredients

  • 10 big scallops, cleaned
  • Salt
  • Black pepper, ground
  • Olive oil
  • Butter
  • 2 cloves of unpeeled garlic
  • 2 sprigs thyme
  • Lemon

Instructions

Pat the scallops dry. Really really dry. And then some. Let them sit on paper towels for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper from both sides (or do the other side in the pan).
Squish garlic with the flat side of the knife. Prepare two generous cubes of butter and the thyme.
Get a pan very hot, 7-9. Non-stick pan is the easiest, cast-iron second, steel is the most difficult.
Add a bit of olive oil into the pan, spread it a bit and wait briefly for it to get hot, then place the scallops into the pan so that they don’t touch.
They will stick initially, but trust the process. Let them develop a crust, then start gently prodding them to see if they are ustuck yet. They need about 2-3 minutes. Be careful not to tear them. Once unstuck, flip them to the other side and reduce the heat to medium.
Add the butter, garlic and thyme. Tilt the pan and baste (scoop the sauce over) the scallops with the sauce for 1-2min. The butter should be browned.
Serve immediately with lemon juice to taste. Can be served on a bed of pea purree.
